knownDefect.reason: iOS framework-layer hardcode, not filed - this declaration IS the documentation. The C++ constant is "Restart" (native/libs/sdc/barcode/main/include/sdc/barcode/generated_default_constants.hh:142-144) and Android wires BarcodeCountViewDefaults::restartButtonText through, but BarcodeCountMappingFlowSettingsDefaults.swift:21 hardcodes the lowercase "restart" with the comment `// option not available in ios`. The sibling buttons in the same struct all bridge to their C++ constants correctly, so this is an oversight rather than a deliberate iOS-only string; a user-visible button label differs between platforms as a result.

knownDefect.reason: Deliberate iOS framework-layer override of a native default, not filed. FrameworksBarcodePickViewDefaults.swift:39 hardcodes `"hardwareTriggerEnabled": true,  // Always enabled on iOS` instead of reading BarcodePickViewSettingsDefaults, whose C++ value is false (native/libs/sdc/barcode/main/include/sdc/barcode/generated_default_constants.hh:220-222). Deliberate on the iOS side, but still a framework layer contradicting the native default it claims to expose - which is exactly what this drift test exists to surface, so it is recorded rather than papered over. Android reads the native false and matches the SoT.

knownDefect.reason: iOS SDK copy-paste bug, NOT filed as of SDC-33331 - this declaration IS the documentation. -[SDCBarcodePickViewSettingsDefaults showTorchButton] (native/libs/sdc/barcode/ios/src/SDCBarcodePickViewSettingsDefaults.mm:89-91) returns BarcodePickViewSettingsDefaults::showPauseButton() instead of showTorchButton(). The two C++ constants differ: showTorchButton() is false (native/libs/sdc/barcode/main/include/sdc/barcode/generated_default_constants.hh:208-210), showPauseButton() is true (:199-201). CONSEQUENCE, and why this is a real defect rather than a documentation quirk: iOS ships BarcodePick with a torch button VISIBLE by default that is specified to be hidden. Android reads the right constant and matches the SoT, hence platforms: [ios]. Fixing the .mm accessor is what removes this declaration.

iOS coverage gap, not filed. FrameworksBarcodePickViewDefaults.swift:38 emits `"uiButtonsOffset": nil,  // doesn't exist in iOS` - the property was never bridged to the iOS SDK (no uiButtonsOffset in native/libs/sdc/barcode/ios public headers), so the key is present in the dump but valueless while native says {value: 32, unit: dip}. Android bridges it and matches the SoT, hence platforms: [ios]. Bridging the property on iOS is what removes this declaration.
